storm.combination_name: Storm 1.0, the graph network and its Allen–Dynes route, averaged
storm.gnn: graph network 2.0 (weight averaging + Allen–Dynes head + crystal descriptors)

check.about: out of fold on the conventional 3DSC materials that Alexandria also has: of those given at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others

rule: only our own finds: nothing that SuperCon, 3DSC, the Alexandria or JARVIS electron-phonon data or our list of others' claims already has, and nothing made of exactly the elements of a known superconductor
caveat: Storm predicts the DFT (Allen-Dynes, μ* = 0.10) Tc of a structure that DFT says is stable or nearly so; a candidate is a prediction until a full electron-phonon calculation and then an experiment check it

check.about: out of fold on the 3DSC entries: of the compounds Hurricane gave at least an even chance, the share that superconduct, against the share among the others; 31 of the 619 entries lie outside the training part of their fold and get no chance

jackknife.about: every candidate is scored by five models, each trained without one fifth of the training compounds (whole parent compounds) and one fifth of the background; the chance shown is their mean, and the spread is the range between the lowest and the highest of the five

reliability.about: false alarms: the share of held-out background compounds (JARVIS-DFT compounds with no superconductivity record that Radar sends to Hurricane) given at least an even chance of superconducting; an upper bound, as a few of them may superconduct
reliability.cite: T. Konno et al., Phys. Rev. B 103, 014509 (2021)
reliability.parent_about: a parent compound is one Materials Project structure in 3DSC with all the SuperCon entries matched to it: it counts as superconducting if any of them does, and its Tc is the highest they reach
reliability.electronic_about: what the DFT calculation says about the parent's electrons: the band gap, whether it is a metal, the magnetic moment per volume, whether it is magnetic, the distance above the convex hull and the formation energy per atom; from the Materials Project for the training parents and from JARVIS-DFT for the screening pool
reliability.found_about: found: trained without a whole family, the share of that family's superconducting parents given at least an even chance, averaged over the families left out
reliability.dismissed_about: called unlikely: trained without a whole family, the share of that family's superconductors given a chance under one half, averaged over the four families; a compound that gets no chance (not known) is not counted as called unlikely
reliability.unknown_about: not known: a compound further from every training compound, in the model's standardized inputs, than the given multiple of the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound gets no chance

steps.step: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull
a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not
2 to 5 elements, no hydrogen, noble gases or short-lived radioactive elements
up to 40 atoms in the cell
only elements in at least 20 of Hurricane's training materials

pool.rule: within 50 meV/atom of the convex hull, a band gap of at most 1 eV, magnetic or not, 2 to 5 elements, up to 40 atoms in the cell, elements Hurricane's training data covers; the list holds the 354 that Radar sends to Hurricane, one per chemical system, except the 206 too far from Hurricane's training data for it to give a chance

not_known.about: Hurricane gives no chance to a compound further from every training compound, in its standardized inputs, than the distance that separates 95% of the training compounds from their nearest neighbour in another parent compound; such compounds are not listed

hurricane.caveat: Hurricane learned measured Tc from cuprates, iron-based, heavy-fermion compounds and other oxides; it gives the chance that a compound superconducts and its Tc if it does. Many of these compounds would need doping or pressure, and a candidate is a prediction until an experiment checks it
